**CATEGORIFIED ALGEBRA AND QUANTUM MECHANICS**

*JEFFREY MORTON*

68 pp, 29 sections.

**Abstract.** Interest in combinatorial interpretations of mathematical entities stems from the convenience of the concrete models they provide. Finding a bijective proof of a seemingly obscure identity can reveal unsuspected signiﬁ- cance to it. Finding a combinatorial model for some mathematical entity is a particular instance of the process called “categoriﬁcation”. Examples include the interpretation of N as the Burnside rig of the category of ﬁnite sets with product and coproduct, and the interpretation of N[x] as the category of com- binatorial species. This has interesting applications to quantum mechanics, and in particular the quantum harmonic oscillator, via Joyal’s “species”, a new generalization called “stuﬀtypes”, and operators between these, which can be represented as rudimentary Feynman diagrams for the oscillator.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 2 Structure Types; 2.1 Categorification of N and N [[z]]; 3 Structure Types and the Harmonic Oscillator; 3.1 The Quantum Harmonic Oscillator; 3.2 Structure Types and the Weyl Algebra; 4 Stuff Types; 4.1 Groupoids; 4.2 Stuff Types as a Generalization of Structu; 4.3 Stuff Types As Power Series; 4.4 Forgetful Functors: Properties, Structure,; 5 Stuff Types And Quantum Mechanics; 5.1 Inner Product of Stuff Types; 5.2 Stuff Operators; 5.3 Feynman Diagrams and Stuff Operators; 6 M-Stuff Types And Quantum Mechanics; 6.1 M-Stuff Types
